payload.executive_summary: Candidate B1B delivers a Markdown-to-static-site generator using a monolithic CLI pipeline (O1). The plan follows a thin-slice milestone strategy: Milestone 1 produces a minimal but deployable static site (CLI skeleton, Markdown ingestion, single-note HTML rendering), and each subsequent milestone layers on tags, internal links/backlinks, full-text search, and polish. This architecture minimises upfront design overhead and yields a working artifact from the first milestone, de-risking integration. Key risks around link conventions (K2) and tag conventions (K3) are addressed by requiring explicit configuration before the milestones that depend on them. Scale risks (K4/K5) are deferred as acceptable at the confirmed 1,000-note target. Privacy risk (K8) is accepted with documentation-only mitigation. The candidate targets all 14 MUST requirements and covers SHOULD requirements progressively in later milestones.

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 (monolithic CLI pipeline) is the simplest architecture that satisfies every MUST requirement with minimal upfront design. A single-process, in-memory pipeline keeps the codebase small, debuggable, and easy to package. The confirmed target scale of ~1,000 notes (R22) fits comfortably within in-memory processing limits, so the scalability trade-offs of O1 are acceptable. The thin-slice delivery strategy pairs naturally with O1 because each pipeline stage (scan → parse → graph → render → emit) can be built and tested incrementally. The main trade-off—limited extensibility compared to O2's plugin architecture—is acceptable given the project's focused scope and single-user orientation. If extensibility needs grow, the monolith can be refactored toward O2 later without discarding work.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: CLI Orchestrator (C1) → Source Scanner & Front Matter Parser (C2) discovers .md files and extracts front matter → Content Analyzer & Graph Builder (C3) parses links/tags, builds NoteGraph with forward links, backlinks, and tag associations → Markdown Renderer (C4) converts each note to HTML → Template & Theme Renderer (C5) produces per-note pages, tag index, per-tag pages, home page, all-notes page → Search Index Builder (C6) generates client-side search index from NoteGraph → Output Emitter (C7) writes HTML, CSS, JS, search index, and static assets to output directory → Client-Side Runtime (C8) loads search index in browser and provides search UI.

milestones.name: CLI Skeleton + Markdown Ingestion + Single-Note HTML Render

Static HTML/CSS/JS output with no server-side runtime dependency (R2)
Build success/failure reporting with actionable error messages (R6)
Graceful handling of malformed YAML front matter (per-file skip with warning, not build failure) (K6)
Default HTML sanitization in renderer to mitigate XSS (K7)

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be used?
decision_log.rationale: O1 is the simplest architecture satisfying all MUST requirements. The confirmed ~1,000-note scale fits in-memory processing. A single-process pipeline is easiest to debug, package, and deliver incrementally. Limited extensibility is an acceptable trade-off for the project's focused scope.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Plugin-based build core: higher upfront complexity for extensibility not yet needed
O3 — Existing SSG (e.g., Eleventy): ties project to external SSG upgrade cadence and complicates standalone distribution
O4 — Multi-stage pipeline with intermediate artifacts: adds disk I/O overhead and cache management complexity unnecessary at this scale
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement for third-party plugin ecosystem or user-authored plugins
Scale growing well beyond 1,000 notes requiring incremental/cached builds
Need to distribute as an SSG theme/config rather than a standalone tool

evidence_pointers.quote: The monolithic CLI pipeline (O1) is the simplest architecture that satisfies all MUST requirements

decision_log.question: What milestone delivery strategy should be used?
decision_log.choice: Thin-slice: each milestone produces a deployable static site with incrementally more features
decision_log.rationale: Thin-slice delivery de-risks integration by producing a working end-to-end artifact from M1. Each subsequent milestone adds a feature vertical (tags, links, search, polish) that can be independently tested and demonstrated.
alternatives_considered: Layer-cake: build all backend pipeline stages first, then add UI/templates — delays feedback
Big-bang: single milestone delivering everything — high integration risk
what_would_change_this_decision: Tight deadline requiring parallel workstreams on independent feature slices
Multiple developers needing to work on isolated components simultaneously

decision_log.question: How should tag conventions be handled given unconfirmed Q2?
decision_log.choice: Support configurable tag sources (YAML front matter and inline #tags) with a normalization pipeline (case-fold, trim, deduplicate)
decision_log.rationale: Making tag source configurable addresses assumption A3 and mitigates K3. Normalization prevents duplicate tags. Configuration must be set before M2 starts.
alternatives_considered: Support only YAML front matter tags — simpler but excludes inline-tag users
Support only inline #tags — misses structured front matter workflows
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms only one tag convention is needed
User requires hierarchical/nested tags (would need additional normalization rules)

decision_log.question: How should internal link conventions be handled given unconfirmed Q1?
decision_log.choice: Default to standard Markdown relative links (R9 MUST); support optional wiki-link syntax via configuration (R15 SHOULD)
decision_log.rationale: Standard relative links satisfy the MUST requirement. Wiki-link support is added as configurable to address R15 and mitigate K2. A deterministic resolver with precedence rules avoids ambiguity.
alternatives_considered: Support only wiki-links — breaks standard Markdown workflows
Auto-detect link style — non-deterministic and harder to debug
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms wiki-links are the only convention used
User requires Obsidian-specific link features (embeds, block references)

evidence_pointers.note: R9 MUST resolve standard Markdown relative links
R15 SHOULD support additional link syntaxes

decision_log.question: How should scale/performance risks (K4, K5) be handled?
decision_log.choice: Defer active mitigation; accept in-memory processing as sufficient for confirmed 1,000-note target
decision_log.rationale: The monolithic in-memory approach (O1) handles 1,000 notes comfortably. Adding streaming or caching would increase complexity without proportional benefit at this scale. R22 sets a concrete 500 ms search latency target that will be validated in M4.
alternatives_considered: Implement streaming/chunked processing from the start — over-engineering for current scale
Choose O4 multi-stage pipeline for incremental builds — unnecessary complexity
what_would_change_this_decision: Target scale increases significantly beyond 1,000 notes
Performance testing in M4 reveals search index exceeds acceptable size/latency

evidence_pointers.note: K5 search index performance at scale
R22 500ms search latency target for 1,000 notes

decision_log.question: How should privacy leakage risk (K8) be mitigated?
decision_log.choice: Documentation-only mitigation: build-time warning banner and README disclaimer
decision_log.rationale: Access control is an explicit non-goal. The user is a single author publishing personal notes. A build-time warning and README disclaimer make the exposure risk visible without adding authentication complexity that contradicts project constraints.
alternatives_considered: Add .gitignore-style exclude patterns for sensitive files — partially addressed by R20 file exclusion
Require explicit opt-in per file for publishing — too burdensome for the workflow
what_would_change_this_decision: User indicates notes contain sensitive/private data that must not be published
Deployment target changes to a shared/public environment with untrusted readers

evidence_pointers.note: Auth and access control are non-goals

decision_log.question: How should XSS risk (K7) be mitigated in the Markdown renderer?
decision_log.choice: Default to HTML sanitization in the renderer; disallow raw HTML unless explicitly opted in via configuration
decision_log.rationale: Since the output is a static site potentially served publicly, sanitizing rendered HTML by default prevents XSS from user content. An opt-in escape hatch preserves flexibility for advanced users who understand the trust model.
alternatives_considered: Allow all raw HTML by default — unacceptable security posture for a publishable site
Strip all HTML with no opt-in — too restrictive for power users
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms notes are strictly private and never shared — could relax default
User requires embedded scripts/widgets in notes — would need a safe-list approach

supplemental_evaluations.title: Acceptance Test Coverage for SHOULD Requirements
supplemental_evaluations.notes: The canonical acceptance tests (AT1–AT14) cover all MUST requirements. SHOULD requirements R15 (wiki-links), R16 (tag normalization), R17 (navigation), R18 (broken-link warnings), R19 (base URL), R20 (file exclusion), R21 (GFM), and R22 (search performance) are addressed in milestones M2–M5 but lack dedicated acceptance tests. Per the branch acceptance strategy, additional tests for these SHOULD requirements should be authored before freeze. Alignment warning AL001 specifically calls out missing tests for wiki-links, tag normalization, navigation, and broken-link handling.

evidence.note: AL001 flags missing SHOULD-requirement test coverage

supplemental_evaluations.title: Governance Posture Alignment
supplemental_evaluations.notes: The branch specifies sandboxed tooling and medium HITL strictness. The risk governance canonical artifact's tool policy restricts all stages to artifact_read/artifact_write with no external network access, which aligns with sandboxed tooling. Medium HITL strictness means human review is required for security decisions (K7, K8, K19), unconfirmed blocker questions (Q1–Q4, Q10), and any scope changes, but routine milestone exits can proceed with automated test gates.

evidence.note: Tool policy restricts to artifact_read/write, no external network

synthesis_warnings.summary: Blocker questions Q1 (link conventions), Q2 (tag conventions), Q3 (scale), Q4 (information architecture), and Q10 (CLI vs GUI) remain unconfirmed. Milestones M2 and M3 cannot start without Q1/Q2 answers. The plan assumes CLI (Q10) and 1,000-note scale (Q3) based on capsule context, but these should be explicitly confirmed before M1 exit.

Alignment warning AL001 identifies missing acceptance tests for SHOULD requirements (R15–R22). New acceptance test IDs (AT15+) would need to be minted, which is outside the allowed ID prefixes for this role. Routing to acceptance test authoring is needed before freeze.

evidence.note: AL001 flags missing SHOULD-requirement acceptance tests

synthesis_warnings.summary: K6 (malformed YAML front matter) has no formal mitigation text in the risk register. M1 deliverable DL6 addresses it with graceful per-file error handling, but the risk register entry should be updated with a mitigation plan for consistency.
